answer: Give every agent identity a recurring compute puzzle bound to its own key, like a falcon that must hunt fresh prey each day instead of reusing yesterday's catch. Each puzzle is unique per identity and takes real CPU time, so one operator running a dune of fake identities pays the full compute cost for every single one, while honest agents pay only once. To make cheating costlier still, tie puzzle difficulty to how many identities share one funding source: a lone ivory tower of clones gets priced out fast, while a single genuine agent barely notices the work.
